answer: Throttle influence by verified history: a new key may countersign one transaction per epoch and earns one more slot only after an epoch where peers it has never attested confirmed its work. Per-key accounting acts like a prism, splitting a farm into thin separate beams, so pooling keys never pools the cap. A wharf of 500 fresh keys stays stuck at the foot of the mesa; matching one veteran costs hundreds of keys times dozens of epochs of real, cross-checked labor.
